method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Genetics, attack phenotype, amyloidosis, etanercept, and IL-1 are all in this review.

mcqs.question: Which gene is mutated in TRAPS?

options.A: TNFRSF1A, encoding TNF receptor 1, with dominant inheritance

mcqs.correctAnswerText: TNFRSF1A, encoding TNF receptor 1, with dominant inheritance
mcqs.explanation: TRAPS is caused by pathogenic variants in TNFRSF1A on chromosome 12, encoding TNF receptor 1, and the pattern is consistent with dominant inheritance.

sourceRefs.excerpt: pathogenic variants in the TNF receptor superfamily member 1A (TNFRSF1A ) gene on chromosome 12, which encodes the TNF (tumor necrosis factor) Receptor 1

mcqs.question: Which clinical picture does the review give for a typical attack?

options.A: Fever sometimes lasting weeks, with abdominal pain, myalgia, arthralgia, migratory erythematous rash, and eye inflammation
options.B: Brief 2-hour fevers without rash or pain
options.D: Chronic destructive arthritis as the only feature

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Fever sometimes lasting weeks, with abdominal pain, myalgia, arthralgia, migratory erythematous rash, and eye inflammation
mcqs.explanation: The disease is characterized by recurrent fever attacks, sometimes lasting weeks, with severe abdominal pain, myalgia, arthralgia, migratory erythematous rash, and eye inflammation. The CNS is typically spared.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The disease is characterized by recurrent fever attacks, sometimes lasting for weeks, accompanied by severe abdominal pain, myalgia, arthralgia, migratory erythematous rash, and eye inflammation, but typically the central nervous system (CNS) is spared

mcqs.question: Why does the review say high serum amyloid A matters?

options.A: It predisposes to AA amyloidosis, historically a severe source of morbidity and mortality
options.C: It is the treatment target for etanercept dosing only
options.D: It causes the rash directly and has no renal consequence

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It predisposes to AA amyloidosis, historically a severe source of morbidity and mortality
mcqs.explanation: Some patients have extremely high serum amyloid A, predisposing them to AA amyloidosis, which was a severe consequence before molecular characterization.

sourceRefs.excerpt: some can have extremely high levels of serum amyloid A (SAA) predisposing them to AA amyloidosis

mcqs.question: What does the review say about etanercept in TRAPS?

options.A: It was only partially beneficial at suppressing symptoms
options.B: It is curative in nearly all patients
options.C: It is contraindicated because it worsens amyloidosis in every series
options.E: It replaces the need for any genetic test

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It was only partially beneficial at suppressing symptoms
mcqs.explanation: Etanercept was only partially beneficial in suppressing TRAPS symptoms, which the authors take as evidence that the shedding hypothesis is only one mechanism.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Etanercept was only partially beneficial in suppressing TRAPS symptoms

mcqs.question: Which cytokine does the review say plays an essential pathogenic role, based on normalization of gene expression after canakinumab?
mcqs.explanation: Fifteen days after canakinumab, elevated TNFRSF1A, IL-1β, MAPK14, and NFKB1 expression normalized. The authors conclude that IL-1β plays an essential role in TRAPS pathogenesis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: This suggests that IL-1β plays an essential role in the TRAPS pathogenesis
